title: Packed-weight inference path specs — low-bit kernels and KV interop
content:
Purpose:

This is a working-spec for the low-bit (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) execution path that describes kernel contracts, packed-weight layouts, scheduler expectations, and KV-cache interaction constraints. Goal: define clear runtime invariants so we can safely route requests to low-bit kernels, provide automatic fallbacks, and ensure KV cache coherence across mixed-precision execution.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: forward-pass inference for decoder and encoder-decoder transformer layers (attention + MLP path), weight packing/layout, per-layer kernel ABI, runtime flags for quantized variants, scheduling heuristics for batching and KV cache reuse.
- Out of scope: training-time quantization-aware transformations, offline weight conversion tooling (covered elsewhere), profiler microbenchmarks (we'll reference results).

Background/assumptions:
- We support multiple quant formats in the runtime: symmetric INT8, asymmetric INT8 (scale+zp), FP8 (E4M3/E5M2 variants), GPTQ (per-tensor/per-channel groupwise quant with codebook/residuals), AWQ-style quant (blockwise scales + correction terms).
- Model artifacts provided by model onboarding pipeline will include metadata: quant-format, weight-shape, packing-version, per-layer scale tables, dequant-stub rules. Runtime must validate metadata before scheduling.

High-level constraints (key requirements):
1) Deterministic inference fallback: if a low-bit kernel is unavailable or incompatible with the current KV or batch shape, the scheduler can fall back to a compatible higher-precision kernel (e.g. FP16) with a clear cost delta.
2) KV cache binary compatibility: KV cache layout produced by a kernel must be consumable by any kernel that declares compatibility for the same layout and precision (compatibility layers must be explicit).
3) Memory alignment: packed-weight blobs must align to 64-byte boundaries for DMA-friendly copy paths; kernels can assume this alignment unless flagged otherwise in metadata.
4) Minimal runtime unpacking: kernels should operate on packed formats in-place where possible; copying or expanding to FP32 is allowed only during fallback and must be accounted for in scheduling.

Kernel ABI / Contract (per-layer):
- Input signature (in-order): {input_ids_tensor, attention_mask?, position_ids?, kv_state_handle?, aux_flags}
- Model layer descriptor: layer_id (string), op_type (self_attn | cross_attn | feedforward), seq_len (int), batch_size (int), num_heads (int), head_dim (int), dtype_hint (int8 | fp8-e4m3 | fp8-e5m2 | gptq | awq | fp16), weight_blob_id (string)
- Weight blob requirements: pointer, packed_layout_version, scale_table_ref (optional), block_size (if blockwise), backup_fp16_blob_id (optional)
- KV handle contract: opaque handle but runtime-enforced metadata must specify kv_layout_version, key_dtype, value_dtype, stride, memory_owner (ephemeral | shared), allows_cross_kernel_use (bool)
- Return values: output_tensor (dtype==execution dtype unless flagged), updated_kv_handles (list), perf_tokens (latency/cost counters)

Packed-weight layout rules (non-normative):
- Base rule: layout = [subblock-headers] + contiguous packed weight payload
- Subblock header (per block): {block_id:uint16, row_count:uint16, scale_index:uint16, reserved:uint16}
- For GPTQ/AWQ: payload includes compressed weight indices followed by residual correction tables. Runtime must provide a decompress helper if kernel cannot operate on compressed indices directly.
- For FP8: store exponent-bias metadata per-tensor; kernels that implement fused dequant can apply exponent correction while loading if flagged.

KV cache interaction patterns and constraints:
1) Shared KV layout versioning: KV caches are versioned. A layer's kernel declares acceptable kv_layout_versions. The scheduler must never place a request in a plan where kernel A writes a KV in layout v1 and kernel B expects v2 unless a compatibility shim is registered.
2) Zero-copy path: when both kernel and KV memory owner are 'shared' and alignment matches, kernel may operate directly on KV memory (significant perf win). Otherwise, a copy-to-local path is used and accounted for in scheduling.
3) Quantized KV storage: we allow quantized storage for keys/values to save memory. If KV is stored quantized, only kernels that can consume that quant format are eligible for routing. Converting cached KV from quant->fp16 on-demand is allowed as a fallback but is expensive and should be avoided except for canary rollouts.
4) KV eviction and version staleness: when rolling out a model variant with different head_dim or block_size, runtime must evict incompatible KV or maintain parallel caches keyed by model variant id.

Scheduling rules and heuristics:
- Eligibility checks (fast): dtype_hint matches kernel capabilities; seq_len within kernel-optimized range; batch_size >= kernel_min_batch (some fused kernels require minimum batch); kv_layout compatible. These checks are O(1) and run in scheduler hot path.
- Cost model inputs: token_latency_estimate, per-request copy-cost (when KV copy needed), dequant-overhead (CPU/GPU memcpy + compute), memory pressure score.
- Batching heuristic: prefer grouping requests with same quant metadata and similar seq_len. When mixed quant types cannot be grouped, group by fallback target (e.g. all FP16 fallbacks together).
- Canary rollouts: for newly onboarded packed-weight blobs, schedule a small percentage of requests to the new kernel with per-request tracing enabled; enforce automatic rollback if per-token quality or error rate regression crosses threshold.

Fallback & compatibility matrix (summary):
- Best-case: kernel supports exact quant format + kv layout -> route.
- Compatible degradations (allowed): AWQ-blockwise -> INT8-per-channel (with dequant on the fly) if scale metadata present; GPTQ (codes+residuals) -> FP16 via decompress path.
- Not allowed: FP8-e5m2 blob -> INT8 kernel (different exponent semantics) unless offline conversion provided and manifest updated.
- The compatibility matrix is encoded in a runtime table mapping (weight_blob.packing_version, kernel_capabilities) -> action (route | convert_offline | runtime_unavailable).

Instrumentation & telemetry required:
- Emit per-request routing decisions: chosen_kernel, rejected_kernels, reason_codes
- KV-copy counters and byte counts (zero-copy vs copied)
- Dequant/pack/unpack microsecond timers
- Quality proxies: for low-bit kernels enable lightweight checks that compare a short sample of outputs against a trusted FP16 baseline on a small fraction of requests (A/B) to detect drift.

Testing / validation plan:
- Unit tests: kernel ABI conformance harness that validates header parsing, scale table lookup, and small matrix-multiply golden outputs against CPU reference.
- Integration tests: mixed-precision pipeline where some layers are low-bit and others are FP16; verify KV layout compatibility and per-token deterministic outputs for canonical prompts.
- Performance smoke: measure copy overhead, memory align edge cases, and batching thresholds on real GPU instances for each kernel variant.
- Chaos tests: simulate unavailable kernel, incompatible KV layout, and ensure graceful fallback with bounded latency spike.

Migration and rollout notes:
- Migration strategy: stage 1 (internal): enable new packed layout on a dev cluster with synthetic load; stage 2: enable canary in prod for <1% traffic with aggressive telemetry; stage 3: ramp if errors < thresholds.
- Backwards compatibility: keep FP16 backup blobs for every quantized onboarding artifact until 2 safe production campaigns complete.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Q: Do we want per-request desired_quality_hint (low/medium/high) so scheduler can accept degraded kernels for low quality but fast latency? TODO: discuss with product.
- Q: Should KV caches be sharded by block_size or by head_dim? TODO: tradeoff doc and memory eval.
- TODO: Define canonical binary format versioning semantics and an upgrade path for offline conversion tools.
- TODO: Add explicit error codes for incompatibility reasons so client-facing telemetry can be filtered.

Notes to self / implementation sketches:
- Implement a lightweight kernel capability registry (json manifest loader) that exposes fast-check bitmask for dtype support, max_seq_len, min_batch, kv_layouts_supported.
- Add small utility to translate AWQ/GPTQ compressed payload into an intermediate uncompressed block for kernels that don't handle codes natively (keep it optional behind flag).
- When copying KV for a fallback, pin and reuse temporary GPU buffers to avoid repeated allocation penalties.

References & prior art:
- AWQ paper and implementation notes (linked in onboarding docs), GPTQ conversion repo, internal perf notes (see linked artifacts).

Appendix: quick compatibility shorthand (human readable)
- FP16 kernels: universal fallback, slower than native low-bit but robust.
- INT8-per-channel: good memory/latency tradeoff; requires scale table and per-out-block dequant path if interacting with FP8 caches.
- FP8: requires strict exponent semantics; prefer kernels that support fused exponent-correction on load.
- GPTQ/AWQ: high compression; expect decompress overhead unless kernel implements direct codebook lookup and fused matmul.

End of draft.

Checklist before merging to spec branch:
- [ ] Add canonical json schema for weight_blob metadata and publish to model onboarding.
- [ ] Implement kernel capability registry and unit tests.
- [ ] Create small integration on dev cluster demonstrating zero-copy quantized KV path.
- [ ] Add per-request routing telemetry to prod tracing pipeline.

(If you’re reading this and have offline conversion scripts or packing helpers, drop a note in #eng-serving-runtime and link the artifacts.)
